newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian court sends former SS major Hass to trial.
newsitem.headline: Italian court sends former SS major Hass to trial.

text.p: A military court ruled on Friday that former German SS major Karl Hass, accused of war crimes in Italy, should stand trial in Rome on April 14.

Judicial sources said it was possible that the initial hearing, in a high-security courtroom inside Rome's Rebibbia prison, could decide to merge Hass's trial with the re-trial of former SS captain Erich Priebke.
Both men are accused of complicity in multiple murder for their roles in the massacre of 335 men and boys at the Ardeatine Caves near Rome on March 24, 1944.
Seventy-five of the victims were Jews.
A date for Priebke's re-trial has not yet been set officially but defence lawyers expected it to start on April 14 or the following day.

Hass, 84, has been under house arrest at a private clinic near Rome since last June when he fractured his pelvis trying to clamber over a hotel balcony and flee the city. He was not in court on Friday.
Hass had returned to Italy to give testimony as a witness at Priebke's original trial.
Priebke is held at a military prison in Rome. He has been jailed since November 1995 when he was extradited from Argentina, where he had lived openly since 1948.
At Priebke's first trial which ended in August last year, a military court found Priebke guilty but freed him, citing circumstances which triggered an expired statute of limitations.
He was rearrested that night after relatives of the massacre victims and other protesters laid siege to the courthouse. The August verdict was quashed on appeal in October.
The Court of Cassation, Italy's highest court, has ruled that a military tribunal should hear Priebke's re-trial instead of a civilian court as families of the victims had wanted.
Priebke, 83, admits shooting two victims and crossing names off a list but said he had to follow orders or be killed himself. Hass has also admitted a role in the massacre.
